title: Deep muscles of the posterior leg (posterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Lateral surface of the lateral condyle of the femur.
Posterior surface of the tibia above the soleal line.
Unlocks the fully extended knee by rotating the femur laterally on the fixed tibia. Weakly flexes the leg at the knee.
Medial part of the posterior surface of the tibia, below the soleal line.
Bases of the distal phalanges of the lateral four toes.
Flexes the lateral four toes. Helps plantarflex the foot and support the longitudinal arches.
Interosseous membrane and the adjoining posterior surfaces of the tibia and fibula.
Tuberosity of the navicular, with slips to the cuneiforms, the cuboid, and the bases of the second to fourth metatarsals.
Plantarflexes and inverts the foot. It is the main muscular support of the medial longitudinal arch.
hy: Behind the medial malleolus, from front to back: Tibialis posterior, flexor Digitorum longus, posterior tibial Artery and Vein, tibial Nerve, flexor Hallucis longus (Tom, Dick And Very Nervous Harry).

rows: Lower two-thirds of the posterior surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe.
Flexes the great toe, which gives the final push-off in walking. Helps plantarflex the foot and support the medial longitudinal arch.
Head and upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
Base of the first metatarsal and the medial cuneiform. Its tendon passes behind the lateral malleolus and crosses the sole in the groove of the cuboid.
Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes it. Supports the transverse arch of the foot.
Lower two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula.
Tuberosity on the base of the fifth metatarsal.
Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes it.
hy: In a forced inversion of the foot its pull can tear the tuberosity off the base of the fifth metatarsal (avulsion fracture).
